results.text: {"level": "crawl", "reason": "Costs are split monthly by gut feel from aggregate invoices, with no tagging, usage-based attribution, or repeatable allocation method."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes monthly invoice reads and gut-feel splitting between teams, with no key-to-owner map or weekly coverage figure, so neither the walk nor the run artefacts are evidenced."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Every API key maps to a named owning team and coverage is reported weekly, which goes beyond ad hoc tagging, but at 86 percent coverage with no mention of automated enforcement or showback/chargeback accuracy, allocation is not yet fully reliable."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a key-to-owning-team mapping and a posted weekly coverage figure (86 percent), which meets the walk artefacts, but it does not mention reconciling coverage to the invoice or owning and aging the untagged remainder, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Monthly reconciliation to the invoice at 97 percent coverage, with an owner and an ageing report for the untagged remainder, shows systematic allocation practice, but it is not yet at run level, which would require near-complete automated allocation and real-time or continuous attribution."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a monthly reconciliation and an ageing report for the untagged remainder, but it does not mention a key-to-owner map or a weekly coverage figure, which are the required walk artefacts, so the Run requirements cannot be met either."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company attributes spend to teams, which goes beyond crawl, but a claim that ownership is clear does not show that AI costs are tagged, allocated consistently, and shared across teams in an automated, governed way that would qualify as run."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement is a claim about team knowledge ('everyone knows which team owns which spend') and an adjective ('best-in-class') rather than describing a key-to-owner map or a weekly coverage figure, so the walk artefact is not evidenced, and therefore neither is the run artefact."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company has mapped keys to owners and tracks coverage weekly at 90 percent, which goes beyond crawl, but it has not yet reconciled allocation to the invoice, so it lacks the automated, invoice-accurate allocation that marks run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company states it maintains a key-to-owner map and tracks weekly coverage at 90 percent, which meets the walk artefacts, but reconciliation to the invoice is only a future plan, so the run requirement is not met."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company claims 99 percent coverage, but that figure is inflated by parking unattributable spend in a shared platform bucket, which means costs are tagged to a catch-all rather than traced to the teams and models that drive them, so allocation is partially in place but not yet accountable enough to qualify as run."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims 99 percent coverage but describes no key-to-owner map or weekly coverage figure, and it provides no reconciliation to the invoice; its shared bucket owned by the platform team is an unaged catch-all, so no walk or run artefact is evidenced."}
{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company only reviews provider dashboards reactively after a surprise bill, with no proactive, granular, or attributed metering of AI usage."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company relies on provider dashboards only when the bill surprises it, with no gateway log of individual calls and no reconciliation to the invoice, so it lacks both the walk and run artefacts."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "A gateway writing a per-call record with model, tokens, owner and cost gives consistent, attributable metering, but without evidence of automated enforcement, forecasting, or real-time anomaly response it falls short of run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a gateway that writes one record per model call with model, tokens, owner and cost, which matches the walk artefact, but it does not mention any reconciliation of those records to the invoice, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Gateway records are reconciled line by line to the invoice monthly with a defined 0.5 percent tolerance, which is a formal, repeatable process, but it is still a monthly batch check rather than continuous, automated metering with real-time or near-real-time cost attribution."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a monthly line-by-line reconciliation to the invoice within a stated 0.5 percent tolerance, which implies gateway records exist, but it never states that the gateway log holds one record per call, so the walk artefact is not evidenced and the run level (which requires it) cannot be reached."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Tracing platform observability suggests the company captures usage data, but claiming full observability does not confirm that token and cost metering is attributed to teams, products, or features and reconciled against billing, which is what distinguishes walk from run."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a tracing platform and observability in general terms but does not state that a gateway log with one record per call exists, so the walk artefact is not evidenced and the run requirement cannot be reached."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The gateway recording every call and cost, with finance trusting the totals, shows reliable per-call metering, but the statement does not indicate automated attribution to teams, products, or features, or real-time visibility, which would be needed for run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a gateway that records every call and its cost, which satisfies the walk artefact, but it says nothing about reconciling those records line by line to the invoice within a stated tolerance each month, so run is not supported; finance trusting the totals is a claim, not evidence of reconciliation."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "Matching the monthly invoice total only shows aggregate reconciliation, with no evidence of per-team, per-model, or per-request metering, so cost attribution and anomaly detection are not yet possible."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement only claims that monthly totals match the invoice, with no mention of a gateway log holding one record per call, so the walk artefact is not evidenced and neither is the run artefact of line-by-line reconciliation within a stated tolerance."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Tracking cost per token and cost per call shows they measure unit costs, but they are not yet tying those unit costs to business outcomes such as cost per customer, transaction, or revenue, which is what defines the run stage."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes tracking cost per token and cost per call, which are input-level unit costs rather than cost per outcome, and it provides no signed cost-per-outcome artefact for any product, so the walk requirement is not met."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company has a defined unit metric (cost per resolved ticket) with a signed definition, which goes beyond basic spend tracking, but it is not stated whether this metric is automated, tracked over time, or used to drive optimization decisions."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a cost per resolved ticket for one product (the support assistant) with the outcome definition signed by its product owner, which meets the walk artefact; it does not mention failures in the numerator, a distribution, or board-pack reporting across all material products, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The company reports cost per outcome for all six material products with retries and failures included in the numerator, shows both median and 95th percentile, and surfaces the metric in the board pack, which covers the full scope, rigor, and executive visibility expected of mature unit economics."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes cost per outcome for all six material products, with retries and failures in the numerator, reported as median and 95th percentile (a distribution), and carried in the board pack, which meets the run requirement that includes the walk artefact; it does not explicitly mention the owner sign-off required for walk, but the run criterion is treated as satisfied by the stated artefact scope, so this is a point of weakness worth verifying."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "A blanket claim that margins are healthy 'across the board' with no per-feature cost-per-unit tracking, allocation, or evidence suggests unit economics are not yet measured at the level needed to manage them."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement is an unsupported adjective claim ('strong', 'healthy across the board') that does not describe any cost-per-outcome artefact for a product, so neither the walk nor the run requirement is evidenced."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Cost per outcome is tracked for only three of six products, so coverage is partial, though the metric is defined carefully enough to include failures and reaches the board, which goes beyond crawl-stage ad hoc reporting but falls short of run-stage consistent unit economics across the whole portfolio."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes cost per outcome for only three of six products with failures included, but it does not show a signed-off artefact for one product from its owner, and the board sees only a summary rather than a distribution across all material products, so neither walk nor run is evidenced."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company tracks cost per successful task for every product, which is a real unit economics metric, but reporting only averages and excluding retried runs hides the true cost of failures and retries, so it falls short of the granular, fully-loaded view expected at run level."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes an average cost per successful task that excludes retried runs, which does not show a cost-per-outcome artefact signed by a product owner (walk) or failures counted in the numerator as a distribution in the board pack (run)."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The forecast is a flat heuristic (last month's bill plus a fixed twenty percent) with no driver-based modeling, usage-volume linkage, or variance tracking against actuals."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a fixed heuristic (last month's bill plus twenty percent) with no driver-based model and no backtest, so it does not meet the walk artefact requirement."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "A driver-based model with defined inputs (calls, tokens, price, mix) that has been backtested over six months shows structured forecasting, but the 11 percent median error and the lack of evidence of automated, continuously recalibrated forecasts keep it short of run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a driver-based forecast (calls, tokens per call, price, mix) with a six-month backtest and reported median error, which meets the walk artefact, but it says nothing about an error budget, variance split by driver, or a register of changes, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The company manages forecasting with an explicit error budget, decomposes monthly variance by driver, and logs every price or model change in a register, which together show mature, driver-based, change-aware forecasting rather than simple historical extrapolation."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes an error budget, variance split by driver and a register of changes, but it never mentions a driver-based forecast with a backtest, which is the walk artefact that run requires alongside these."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a capability ('advanced predictive analytics') without any evidence of how it is implemented, used, or tied to decisions, which suggests marketing language that is unverified and does not show more than basic or ad hoc forecasting."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims 'advanced predictive analytics' but describes no driver-based forecast or backtest, so it does not evidence the walk artefact, let alone the run artefact."}
{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company has driver-based forecasting and a backtest, which places it beyond crawl, but its planned change register is not yet in place, so it has not reached run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a driver-based forecast with a backtest, which meets the walk artefact, while the planned register of changes is a future intention and does not satisfy the run requirements of an error budget and variance split by driver."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company forecasts by driver and explains variance monthly, which goes beyond crawl-level top-down budgeting, but without backtesting it cannot yet demonstrate forecast accuracy or reliably improve its models, so it falls short of run."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company describes a driver-based forecast with monthly variance explanation, but states it has never backtested the forecast, so the walk artefact (driver-based forecast with a backtest) is not evidenced and the run requirements cannot be met either."}
{"level": "crawl", "reason": "Spend spikes are only noticed in a monthly review meeting, which means detection is manual, retrospective, and too slow to stop cost overruns as they happen."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company describes detecting spend spikes only in a monthly review meeting, which is not a daily alert on spend, so the walk artefact is absent and the run requirements cannot apply."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "A daily threshold alert against a trailing average is a real, automated anomaly signal beyond manual review, but it is a fixed-percentage rule that does not account for seasonality, service-level breakdown, or automated response, which keeps it short of run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a daily spend alert that fires to a channel when spend exceeds 130 percent of the trailing average, which meets the walk artefact, but it says nothing about per-product rating, owners, runbooks, historical replay, or time-to-stop measurement, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "Alerts are tied to unit economics (call-rate and cost-per-session by product), each has an owner and runbook, and the detection and response are validated by replaying 90 days of history and measuring a 14-minute median time to stop, which indicates an automated, measured practice rather than ad hoc monitoring."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes per-product rate alerts (call-rate and cost-per-session) with owners and runbooks, replayed on 90 days of history with a measured 14-minute median time to stop, which satisfies the Run artefact, and it implicitly includes spend alerting, which satisfies Walk."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company claims AI-powered anomaly detection that catches issues before they hit the bill, which implies automated alerting beyond manual review, but the statement gives no evidence of coverage, response workflows, or ownership, so the maturity cannot be confirmed as run-level."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims AI-powered anomaly detection but describes no artefact such as daily spend alerts, per-product rate alerts with owners and runbooks, or replay and time-to-stop measurement, so it cannot be credited with walk or run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company has per-product rate alerts with owners and runbooks, which is more than crawl-stage ad hoc monitoring, but it has never replayed those alerts against historical data to validate their thresholds, which keeps it short of run-stage tuned and continuously validated anomaly detection."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company describes per-product rate alerts with owners and runbooks, which satisfies the walk artefact of daily spend alerts, but states they have never been replayed on history, so the run requirement of replay and measured time-to-stop is not met."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Daily alerts exist and an incident was caught within an hour, but the reliance on someone 'usually' looking suggests detection is manual and inconsistent rather than automated, scoped, and routinely acted on."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes daily alerts firing on spend, which meets the walk artefact, but it does not show per-product alert rates, named owners and runbooks, or history replay, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "Budgets are kept in a spreadsheet and updated only quarterly by finance, with no evidence of real-time tracking, per-team allocation, or automated alerts tied to AI spend."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "Budgets exist only as a spreadsheet updated quarterly, with no evidence of per-team budgets with threshold alerts, let alone gateway-enforced caps, a degradation ladder, or logged exceptions."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Each team has a monthly budget with an 80 percent alert routed to the team lead, which is solid per-team accountability, but there is no mention of forecasting, automated enforcement, or budget-driven optimization that would mark a run-level practice."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes per-team monthly budgets with an alert at 80 percent sent to the team lead, which meets the walk artefact, but it says nothing about caps enforced at the gateway before the call, a degradation ladder, or logged exceptions, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "Caps are enforced preemptively at the gateway before calls are made, with a defined per-product degradation ladder and a weekly exceptions review, which together indicate automated, policy-driven budget control with continuous governance rather than after-the-fact monitoring."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes enforcement, a degradation ladder, and an exceptions log, but it never mentions per-team budgets or an alert at a threshold, which are the walk artefact that the run level requires as a prerequisite, so the walk level is not supported."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "A general claim of 'robust budget controls across the organisation' is unsubstantiated, and without evidence of per-team or per-model AI spend budgets, alerts, and enforcement, it reflects at most ad hoc or aspirational controls."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement is an adjective-based claim ('robust budget controls') that does not describe any artefact, such as per-team budgets with threshold alerts, so it cannot be credited with walk or run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Hard caps enforced in the agent framework configuration, with agents stopping on breach, shows automated, system-level budget control, but without evidence of per-team or per-workflow allocation, forecasting, or anomaly-driven adjustment that would mark a run-level practice."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a per-agent cap written into framework configuration that stops agents on hitting it, but it does not show per-team budgets with threshold alerts (the walk artefact), and enforcement sits in the agent framework rather than before the call at a gateway."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Budgets are partially enforced: hard caps exist for the two largest products at the gateway, but the other five rely only on 80 percent alerts, so enforcement is inconsistent across the portfolio."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes hard caps enforced at the gateway for only two products and 80 percent alerts for the other five, but it does not establish per-team budgets with alert thresholds across teams, nor a degradation ladder or logged exceptions, so the walk artefact is not clearly met and the run requirements are absent."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company pays on-demand for everything and has no reserved capacity, savings plans, or committed-use discounts, so it is not yet using commitments to lower AI spend."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement 'Everything is pay as you go' describes no commitment artefact, so it does not meet the walk requirement of one commitment sized from measured usage, and therefore cannot reach run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company has made a single commitment sized from historical usage at a conservative 70 percent, which shows deliberate, data-informed commitment buying, but it is still one commitment without evidence of ongoing portfolio management, coverage targets, or regular rightsizing."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company bought one commitment sized from measured usage (70 percent of the last three months), which meets the walk artefact, but the statement says nothing about modelling against model-change scenarios or tracking exit terms and shortfall exposure, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Modelling each commitment against three model-change scenarios and tracking shortfall exposure monthly shows structured, recurring governance, but summarising exit terms rather than actively optimising and rebalancing commitments across models falls short of a run-level practice."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims commitments were modelled, exit terms summarised and shortfall tracked, but it does not describe any specific commitment sized from measured usage, so the walk artefact is not evidenced and the run requirements cannot be met."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes negotiating vendor terms in general but mentions no specific commitment instruments (such as reserved capacity, savings plans, or committed-use discounts), no utilization tracking, and no centralized ownership of commitment decisions, which are the marks of a more mature practice."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims strong negotiated terms but describes no commitment sized from measured usage, so the walk artefact is absent and the run artefact cannot be present either."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company sizes its commitment from observed usage, which goes beyond ad hoc purchasing, but planning to model a model change only at renewal indicates reactive, periodic review rather than continuous, forecast-driven commitment management."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company states it has a commitment sized from usage, which meets the walk artefact, but its plan to model a model change at renewal is an intention rather than an existing artefact, so the run requirement is not supported."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company does monthly shortfall modeling, which shows active tracking of commitment exposure, but the commitment was sized from a vendor forecast rather than their own usage data, a gap that a mature practice would have closed."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes monthly shortfall modelling of a commitment sized from a vendor's forecast rather than measured usage, which does not meet the walk artefact requirement of a commitment sized from measured usage, so the highest supported level is crawl."}
{"level": "crawl", "reason": "With no written ownership of who may change a model or a spending cap, governance is informal and ad hoc, which is the starting stage of the crawl phase."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company states that no one has written down who may change a model or a cap, so it does not have the required walk artefact of a written governance policy with a recurring review, and therefore cannot reach walk or run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "A written policy and a regular two-week review by platform and finance leads show defined ownership and recurring oversight, but the statement does not mention automated enforcement, chargeback, or policy-driven controls that would mark a run-level practice."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company describes a written AI cost policy and a recurring review every two weeks by platform and finance leads, which matches the walk artefacts, but nothing indicates policy as code, a reproducible evidence pack, or a gate on model changes, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The company describes cost rules as enforced policy-as-code, evidence packs reproducible from the ledger with a single command, and a mandatory cost-and-quality gate that blocks model changes, which together indicate automated, enforced governance rather than manual or advisory controls."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes all three run artefacts (cost rules as policy as code, an evidence pack rebuilt from the ledger with one command, and a gate on model changes), and it implies the walk artefact of written policy and recurring review, though it does not explicitly state a recurring review."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company's claim of a mature framework is an unsupported assertion with no described policies, ownership, spend-linked controls, or evidence of enforcement, so the capability can only be assessed from what is shown, which is nothing concrete."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement only asserts that the company takes AI governance seriously and has a mature framework; it describes no written policy, recurring review, policy-as-code, evidence pack, or model-change gate, so no artefact for walk or run is evidenced."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "A written policy and regular review show formalized governance, but enforcement relying mostly on convention rather than automated controls places the company beyond crawl without yet reaching run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company describes a written policy and a regular review, which meets the walk artefacts, but the statement says the rules are mostly enforced by convention and does not describe policy as code, a reproducible evidence pack, or a gate on model changes, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "Governance rules are already codified and evidence is reproducible, which goes beyond crawl, but the absence of a gate on model changes means controls are not yet consistently enforced across the full change lifecycle, so it falls short of run."}
